summary: Researchers developed a digital twin framework to safely evaluate the effects of drugs on the immune system and time to labor, which could enable personalized interventions to prevent preterm births.
title: Applying digital twins to prevent preterm births

summary: Preclinical analysis and a phase 1 trial support VG-3927 as a promising drug candidate for Alzheimer’s disease, demonstrating successful penetration of the central nervous system, target engagement and tolerability.
title: A small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease

summary: PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I–IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. Here we report the prespecified secondary endpoint, 5-year iDFS and exploratory circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) findings. After a median follow-up of 5.6 years, the 5-year iDFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 85.7 to 93.4) in group B (n = 267) and 92.4% (95% CI: 86.7 to 98.5) among 18F-FDG-PET responders achieving pCR without chemotherapy (n = 86), with one distant recurrence. The latter estimate describes a long-term outcome in a post-randomization subgroup defined by 18F-FDG-PET response and pCR and should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as causal effects of omitting chemotherapy. Detectable ctDNA at baseline or during treatment was associated with inferior iDFS, whereas ctDNA clearance correlated with higher pCR rates and improved long-term outcomes. These findings continue to support the clinical validity of an 18F-FDG-PET-guided, pCR-adapted approach and suggest a potential role for ctDNA in refining treatment individualization. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03161353 . A 5-year secondary analysis of the phase 2 PHERGain trial supports the clinical utility of a PET-guided adaptive strategy for treatment de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and provides circulating tumor DNA insights that could inform further treatment approaches.
title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial

summary: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment. A multimodal vision language foundation model, EVLF-FM, integrates extensive clinical data and advanced training techniques, achieving superior diagnostic accuracy and explainability across diverse imaging modalities, enhancing clinical decision-making through robust reasoning and interpretability.
title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability

summary: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell–cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology. A high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas of 189 colorectal tumors from patients aged 20–90+ years uncovers age-associated features of colorectal cancer.
title: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum

summary: Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease. This Review examines the cellular, organ-level and whole-body differences between metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity, as well as variations in response to weight loss—with the goal of improving strategies for preventing and treating obesity-related metabolic disorders.
title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity
